items.fromString:
Marketplace-published RHCOS boot images can drift from what MCO supports without any alerting today.

  Proposal:

# Add a monthly Prow periodic, run per active release branch (including master).
# For each branch, fetch all published AWS Marketplace AMIs (via AWS EC2 client, e.g. DescribeImages) for that branch's listing.
# Determine the acceptable version band for that branch:
- Floor: the RHCOS/OCP skew limit (RHCOSVersionBootImageSkewLimit / OCPVersionBootImageSkewLimit in pkg/controller/common/constants.go) as it stood ~4 months ago, reconstructed via git log on those constants. This is to so marketplace folks have some slack to mirror the latest RHEL minor bump to the marketplace. 
- Ceiling: that branch's current pinned RHCOS version, from data/data/coreos/coreos-rhel-10.json on the matching branch of openshift/installer.
# Pass if at least one published AMI falls within the band. Fail if none do.
# On failure, search for an existing open MCO Jira bug for the condition; file a new one only if none exists.
# Repeat for every product code in that branch.

items.fromString:
Marketplace-published boot images can drift from the RHCOS/OCP version MCO currently supports without disabling upgrades. Nothing today alerts us when that drift grows too large.

Proposal:
Add a Prow periodic, running monthly, that:

# Queries the AWS Marketplace AMI via the AWS EC2 client for the currently published boot image version.
# Compares it against MCO's boot image skew limit ({{RHCOSVersionBootImageSkewLimit}} / {{OCPVersionBootImageSkewLimit}} in {{pkg/controller/common/constants.go)}}.
# Uses git log on those constants to find the skew limit as it stood ~4 months ago, and checks whether today's Marketplace image would already have failed against that older limit. We want to give about 4 months of slack for the marketplace folks to bump the image.
# If so, files a Jira bug against the MCO, first checking whether an open bug for this already exists to avoid duplicates.

There is a current initiative to transition documentation from a feature-focused perspective to a jobs-to-be-done perspective. That means, instead of sharing information in terms of disparate features that customers must piece together or connect to their problems themselves, we will start writing documentation in terms of desired outcomes.

This spike is meant to track the work required to provide a software engineer’s perspective of the MCO docs from the new “jobs-to-be-done“ perspective.

*Done when:*

* This form is filled in for the software engineer perspective: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MGfZXq0wrzzSJGp82tFKvRyLRH61wxRLIVlkPAV4VUM/edit?gid=0#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MGfZXq0wrzzSJGp82tFKvRyLRH61wxRLIVlkPAV4VUM/edit?gid=0#gid=0|smart-link] 
* Any perspectives or ideas related to the documentation push are shared with Michael Burke and Matt Werner

*Additional Resources:*

* Source page with information about the “jobs-to-be-done“ perspective: [https://source.redhat.com/projects_and_programs/docs_and_learn/docx~3/docs_as_jtbd|https://source.redhat.com/projects_and_programs/docs_and_learn/docx~3/docs_as_jtbd]
* Presentation on the why behind the doc perspective shift: [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1v4KxzXrdOTRsXe0G55oMGPiy7QrYT--JKhEdPKNoxqE/edit?slide=id.g37d44d46d8b_0_3#slide=id.g37d44d46d8b_0_3|https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1v4KxzXrdOTRsXe0G55oMGPiy7QrYT--JKhEdPKNoxqE/edit?slide=id.g37d44d46d8b_0_3#slide=id.g37d44d46d8b_0_3|smart-link]

items.fromString:
This spike aims to uncover what is required from the MCO to integrate with the next-gen integrated image registry. Specifically, we need to answer the following questions:

* How can we determine whether the internal image registry is running?
* How can we authenticate to the internal image registry using a service account token?
* How to perform image signing as part of OCL?
* How we can verify image signature before applying the new image?



*Done When:*

* The above questions are answered and additional Jira cards are opened and assigned to the parent epic ([https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MCO-2398|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MCO-2398])

items.toString: This work item links to "https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/4878 (Web Link)"
This work item is depended on by CORENET-5972

With the introduction of [https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/6010|https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/6010|smart-link]  , the MCO verifies the on disk state of the extensions pre-upgrade. While this is the expected behaviour, the MCO can’t account for package changes in between versions (i.e. a difference in the list of packages underlying the extension), causing it to fail validation since the new MCD rolls out before the update happens.

We should have a mechanism to generically specify changes to a MCD version so it understands what previous MCDs most likely have written. This can be a list alongside the extensions list so our verification methods understand that diff. We should also remove the changes 1 release after its introduced (and likely later on, after every EUS version).

For more context, see [https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C02CZNQHGN8/p1782380479590389|https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C02CZNQHGN8/p1782380479590389|smart-link]

items.toString:
Problem: 
As an OpenShift cluster admin, I want to view the real-time status conditions and messages of a MOSB on a paused MCP, So that I can verify that my custom that my MOSB successful before I allow a cluster-wide node rollout.



Background: 
Currently, when spec.paused is set to true on an MCP, the Machine Config Operator, stops reporting the status message of the MOSB even though a change to the MOSC still triggers an underlying MOSB in the background.



Acceptance Criteria:
Given a MachineConfigPool has spec.paused: true, when an admin applies or modifies a MachineOSConfig, then a MachineOSBuild status shows when being built.

As an OpenShift cluster admin, I want to view the real-time status conditions and messages of a MOSB on a paused MCP, So that I can verify that my custom that my MOSB successful before I allow a cluster-wide node rollout.

fields.summary: Expose MachineOSBuild Status Conditions on Paused MachineConfigPools

items.toString:
With [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MCO-1699|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MCO-1699|smart-link] , team MCO introduced the [#trt-alert-mco|https://redhat.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C08SFPGB4NN] Slack. This channel was intended to provide early alerting to the team about component regressions. Now that the channel has been operational for a few releases, we should take the opportunity to understand if the channel is providing the desired value and if any adjustments should be made.

To understand as a team the effectiveness of channel thus far, we should decide as a team what the primary goals of a reporting Slack channel are. Then we should evaluate the pas releases with the channel to see if those goals have been met. Finally, we should be able to clearly document where there may be opportunities to improve the implementation for reporting in the future.

*Done when:*

* There is a clear understanding of the team’s views on the usefulness of the #trt-alert-mco Slack channel
* Stories, bugs, spikes, or epics are refined to represent the desired updates to the channel, if applicable

items.fromString: Investigate options for promoting log running QE suites to report to Component Readiness
items.toString: Investigate options for promoting long running QE suites to report to Component Readiness

There are currently no plans for 5.0 to have the long running QE test suites report to component readiness. However, given the importance of many of the tests in the suite, especially the tests labeled as “Level 0,” we need to develop a plan for how to get the tests reporting. Some concerns about the tests stem from concern that the tests will not pass 100% of the time due to how long they run and infrastructure instability. We need to understand if there are compromises that will allow for the tests to report to component readiness without causing an influx of unnecessary bug reports.

*Done when:*

* There is an understanding between the MCO & testing team on how the long running QE test suites can or should report to component readiness.

items.toString: This work item links to "openshift/origin#31211: MCO-2296: OSImageStreams v1 promotion (Web Link)"

*Story*

As part of [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MCO-2319|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/MCO-2319|smart-link]  we introduced a temporary change to move from direct typed API calls to query for the OSImageStream singleton to a dynamic call that doesn’t require to have the OSImageStream type and the underlying apiVersion of it.

This card covers the simple restore of the direct typed API call and the removal of the dynamic calls the original card introduced.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* OSImageStream get calls are done using the typed methods of client-go
* OSImageStream is expected to be v1
* No tests are removed
This work item is blocked by MCO-2319

items.toString: This work item links to "openshift/origin#31220: MCO-2319: Temporal OSImageStream dynamic call (Web Link)"

*Story*

To bump OSImageStreams from v1alpha to v1 origin, that has OSImageStream usages, needs an API and version bump. Unfortunately, the API bump brings other changes that are not compatible with the vendored kube-apiserver so we need to temporarily replace the OSImageStream API calls with plain dynamic queries till the kubernetes bump happens in origin and we can restore back the direct API call.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Direct typed calls to fetch the OSImageStream singleton are replaces to avoid calling the typed client-go methods
* All existing tests are preserved
